mainTopic: Which relatives the חכמים forbade as שניות: כלת בתו, the wife of the mother's maternal half-brother, and relatives one generation up
overview: The amud opens by fixing רב's list of four women whose rabbinic prohibition (שניות) stops after one generation. After two tries, the גמרא settles that the 'כלה' on the list is כלת בתו, his daughter's daughter-in-law. רב חסדא explains, from a saying of רבי אמי, that she was forbidden only so people would not confuse her with כלת בנו. אביי, רב פפא and רב אשי each name a real family where that mix-up could happen. Next the גמרא asks whether the wife of the mother's maternal half-brother is forbidden. רב ספרא says no, since the Rabbis do not make a גזירה לגזירה, but רבא shows they did exactly that with the grandmothers, the grandfathers' wives and the uncles' wives. Using רב יהודה בר שילא's principle from ארץ ישראל, the גמרא concludes she is forbidden: she is linked through one marriage, while the in-law cases need two. Finally, the wife of the father's father's brother and the father's father's sister are discussed. אמימר permits them, and רב הלל challenges him with a list of sixteen שניות, a debate that continues onto the next amud.

steps.title: One's own daughter-in-law is a Torah prohibition
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא objects to רב listing 'כלתו' among rabbinic prohibitions, since a daughter-in-law is forbidden directly by a פסוק.
steps.simpleTranslation: But that is a Torah prohibition, as it is written: 'You shall not uncover the nakedness of your daughter-in-law'!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא is challenging רב's list. He put 'כלתו' among the rabbinic שניות, but a man's daughter-in-law is forbidden by the תורה.
steps.deeperAnalysis: רב's list is only about rabbinic extensions (שניות) that stop after one generation. A woman forbidden by a פסוק is an ערוה from the תורה, so she does not belong on a rabbinic list at all.

keyTerms.meaning: from the תורה (not rabbinic)
daughter-in-law
a relative forbidden by the תורה
a stopping point: the prohibition does not continue to later generations

steps.confusionAlert: The question 'כלתו?' was asked just before this section. This line is the reason behind that question: a daughter-in-law is a Torah ערוה, not a rabbinic שניה.

phrases.english: It is from the Torah!
phrases.notes: He means 'כלתו' from רב's list, the four women whose rabbinic prohibition stops after one generation.

phrases.english: As it is written: 'The nakedness of your daughter-in-law you shall not uncover'!

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Continues the objection to רב's list of four women whose prohibition has a הפסק (stated before this section).
steps.kashyaTarget: רב's inclusion of 'כלתו' among rabbinic שניות that have a הפסק
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: A plain daughter-in-law is explicitly forbidden by a פסוק, so she cannot be a rabbinic שניה.

steps.title: Read it as his son's daughter-in-law
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא suggests that רב meant כלת בנו, the daughter-in-law of his son.
steps.simpleTranslation: Say: his son's daughter-in-law.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers by changing how we read רב's word. 'כלתו' should be read as כלת בנו, his grandson's wife.
steps.deeperAnalysis: His grandson's wife is not mentioned in the פסוק, so she could be a rabbinic שניה. That would make her fit on רב's list.

keyTerms.meaning: say / read it as
his son's daughter-in-law (his grandson's wife)

phrases.english: Say: his son's daughter-in-law.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the קשיא by rereading רב's term.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Rereading the wording of the statement
steps.terutzHavaAmina: We thought רב meant his own daughter-in-law.
steps.terutzMaskana: רב meant his son's daughter-in-law, who is only rabbinically forbidden.

steps.title: A ברייתא says the son's daughter-in-law has no stopping point
steps.stepSummary: A ברייתא shows that the prohibition of כלת בנו continues through every generation, so it has no הפסק.
steps.simpleTranslation: Does his son's daughter-in-law have a stopping point? But it was taught: his daughter-in-law is an ערוה; his son's daughter-in-law is a שניה; and the same applies to his son and his son's son, until the end of all generations.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא attacks the new reading. A ברייתא says the prohibition on daughters-in-law down the son's line never stops.
steps.deeperAnalysis: רב's list is only for prohibitions that stop. Since the ברייתא extends כלת בנו to every later generation, she cannot be on that list. So the answer in step 2 fails.

keyTerms.meaning: but it was taught in a ברייתא (introduces a source that contradicts)
a secondary relative forbidden by the חכמים
until the end of all generations

phrases.english: And does his son's daughter-in-law have a stopping point?
But it was taught:
His daughter-in-law is a Torah-forbidden relative,
his son's daughter-in-law is a secondary one,

phrases.aramaic: וְכֵן אַתָּה אוֹמֵר בִּבְנוֹ וּבֶן בְּנוֹ
phrases.english: and so you say about his son and his son's son,
phrases.notes: He means their wives too: the wife of a great-grandson, and so on down.

phrases.english: until the end of all generations.

steps.triggerLanguage: וְכַלַּת בְּנוֹ יֵשׁ לָהּ הֶפְסֵק? וְהָא תַּנְיָא
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Challenges the rereading offered in step 2.
steps.kashyaTarget: The reading 'כלת בנו' in רב's list
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: The ברייתא says the prohibition of daughters-in-law down the son's line continues forever, so it has no הפסק.

steps.title: Read it as his daughter's daughter-in-law
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא's final reading: רב meant כלת בתו, the daughter-in-law of his daughter.
steps.simpleTranslation: Rather, say: his daughter's daughter-in-law.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא drops the earlier reading and gives a new one. רב was talking about the wife of his daughter's son.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The ברייתא only extends the son's line forever; it says nothing about the daughter's line. So כלת בתו can be a rabbinic שניה that stops after one generation, which fits רב's list.

keyTerms.meaning: rather (drops the previous answer)
his daughter's daughter-in-law (wife of his daughter's son)

steps.whatToRemember: The 'כלה' on רב's list is כלת בתו. She is forbidden by the חכמים, and that prohibition does not continue to later generations.

phrases.english: Rather, say: his daughter's daughter-in-law.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Replaces the rejected reading from step 2.
steps.terutzMaskana: רב meant כלת בתו, whose rabbinic prohibition does stop.

steps.title: רב חסדא's teaching from רבי אמי
steps.stepSummary: רב חסדא reports that he heard from רבי אמי that one כלה was forbidden only because of another כלה.
steps.simpleTranslation: As רב חסדא said: I heard this from a great man, and who was it? רבי אמי: They forbade a daughter-in-law only because of a daughter-in-law.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא brings support that כלת בתו is rabbinically forbidden. רב חסדא quotes a short, puzzling saying he heard from רבי אמי.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The saying shows that one daughter-in-law was forbidden only as a fence around another one. The next step explains which כלה is which.

keyTerms.meaning: a great man (a great scholar)
I heard
because of

phrases.english: As Rav Ḥisda said:

phrases.aramaic: הָא מִילְּתָא מִגַּבְרָא רַבָּה שְׁמִיעַ לִי,
phrases.english: This matter I heard from a great man,
and who was he? Rabbi Ami:

phrases.aramaic: לֹא אָסְרוּ כַּלָּה אֶלָּא מִפְּנֵי כַּלָּה.
phrases.english: They forbade a daughter-in-law only because of a daughter-in-law.

steps.triggerLanguage: דְּאָמַר רַב חִסְדָּא: הָא מִילְּתָא מִגַּבְרָא רַבָּה שְׁמִיעַ לִי
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Supports the reading 'כלת בתו' from step 4.
steps.raayaObject: That כלת בתו is a rabbinic prohibition
steps.raayaSupportSource: רבי אמי's teaching as reported by רב חסדא

steps.title: רב חסדא works out the meaning himself
steps.stepSummary: Told by astrologers he would be a teacher, רב חסדא figured out the meaning on his own: כלת בתו was forbidden because of כלת בנו.
steps.simpleTranslation: The Chaldeans told me: You will be a teacher. I said: If I become a great man, I will figure it out myself; if I become a children's teacher, I will ask the חכמים who come to the synagogue. Now I have figured it out myself: they forbade his daughter's daughter-in-law only because of his son's daughter-in-law.
steps.whatsHappening: רב חסדא tells a short story about how he came to understand רבי אמי's saying. Then he gives the meaning: כלת בתו is forbidden as a fence for כלת בנו.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Since the son's daughter-in-law is forbidden, the חכמים also forbade the daughter's daughter-in-law so people would not confuse the two. Because she is only a fence, her prohibition does not go further down, and that is exactly the הפסק in רב's list.

keyTerms.meaning: Chaldeans (astrologers)
a teacher
a teacher of young children
from my own understanding

steps.whatToRemember: כלת בתו is forbidden only so that people won't mix her up with כלת בנו, so her prohibition stops after one generation.
steps.whyThisMatters: This explains why כלת בתו has a הפסק and כלת בנו does not: one is the real שניה, the other is only a fence around it.

phrases.english: And the Chaldeans told me: You will be a teacher.
I said: If I become a great man,
I will figure it out on my own;
if I become a teacher of children,
I will ask it of the Sages who come to the synagogue.
Now I have figured it out on my own:

phrases.aramaic: לֹא אָסְרוּ כַּלַּת בִּתּוֹ אֶלָּא מִשּׁוּם כַּלַּת בְּנוֹ.
phrases.english: They forbade his daughter's daughter-in-law only because of his son's daughter-in-law.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Explains the vague saying of רבי אמי quoted in step 5.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: כלת בתו is forbidden by the חכמים only as a fence for כלת בנו.

steps.title: אביי's example: the family of בר ציתאי
steps.stepSummary: אביי shows רבא a real family where the two kinds of daughters-in-law could be confused.
steps.simpleTranslation: אביי said to רבא: I will explain it to you: for example, the daughter-in-law of the house of בר ציתאי.
steps.whatsHappening: אביי gives a real-life example of why a mix-up between כלת בנו and כלת בתו could happen. He points to a known family.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The fence in step 6 only makes sense if people could actually confuse the two. אביי points to a household where this could plainly happen.

keyTerms.meaning: I will explain it to you
for example
of the house (family) of

phrases.english: Abaye said to Rava,
I will explain it to you:
For example, the daughter-in-law of the house of bar Tzitai.

steps.triggerLanguage: אֲמַר לֵיהּ אַבָּיֵי לְרָבָא, אַסְבְּרַהּ לָךְ
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Illustrates the confusion that the decree in step 6 guards against.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: The family of בר ציתאי is an example where the daughters-in-law could be confused.

steps.title: רב פפא's and רב אשי's examples
steps.stepSummary: רב פפא and רב אשי each name another family where the same confusion could arise.
steps.simpleTranslation: רב פפא said: for example, the daughter-in-law of the house of רב פפא בר אבא. רב אשי said: for example, the daughter-in-law of the house of מרי בר איסק.
steps.whatsHappening: Two more אמוראים give their own examples of a family where the mix-up could happen.
steps.deeperAnalysis: These are different examples of the same idea, not an argument about the law. Each one names a household known in his own time.

keyTerms.meaning: the daughter-in-law of

phrases.english: Rav Pappa said:

phrases.aramaic: כְּגוֹן כַּלָּתֵהּ דְּבֵי רַב פָּפָּא בַּר אַבָּא.
phrases.english: For example, the daughter-in-law of the house of Rav Pappa bar Abba.
Rav Ashi said:

phrases.aramaic: כְּגוֹן כַּלָּתֵהּ דְּבֵי מָרִי בַּר אִיסַק.
phrases.english: For example, the daughter-in-law of the house of Mari bar Isak.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Gives other examples parallel to אביי's in step 7.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: Further real families where כלת בנו and כלת בתו could be confused.

steps.title: Is the wife of the mother's maternal half-brother forbidden?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא asks whether the Rabbis' prohibition on uncles' wives reaches the wife of one's mother's half-brother when the two share only a mother. In that case there is no father link at all.
steps.simpleTranslation: They asked: what about the wife of your mother's brother who shares only her mother? The Rabbis forbade the wife of your father's brother from the mother, and the wife of your mother's brother from the father. Both of those have a 'father side.' Maybe that is why the Rabbis decreed on them, and where there is no father side at all they did not decree. Or maybe it makes no difference?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא opens a new question. Does the rabbinic ban on uncles' wives also cover the wife of a mother's half-brother when they share only a mother?
steps.deeperAnalysis: The two uncle's-wife cases already forbidden by the Rabbis each have some link through a father. In the new case, both links (you to your mother, your mother to her brother) run only through mothers. So maybe it is too far removed to be confused with the Torah-level case.

keyTerms.meaning: A question was raised before them (an open question)
A 'father side': some link that runs through a father
Through the mother only (a half-sibling sharing a mother)
Or perhaps there is no difference

steps.confusionAlert: Keep the two 'mother/father' words apart. The first (אחי האם / אחי האב) tells you whose brother it is. The second (מן האם / מן האב) tells you which parent that brother shares with his sibling.

phrases.english: A question was raised before them:

phrases.aramaic: אֵשֶׁת אֲחִי הָאֵם מִן הָאֵם, מַהוּ?
phrases.english: The wife of the mother's brother from the mother, what is the law?
phrases.notes: This is your mother's half-brother who shares only her mother, not her father.

phrases.english: The wife of the father's brother from the mother
and the wife of the mother's brother from the father,
where there is a father side,
that is where the Rabbis decreed;
but where there is no father side,
the Rabbis did not decree about them;
or perhaps there is no difference?

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Moves from the כלה cases to a new question about how far the rabbinic ban on uncles' wives reaches.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: Is the wife of the mother's maternal half-brother a rabbinic שניה, or does the ban need some father link?

steps.title: רב ספרא: we do not add a decree on top of a decree
steps.stepSummary: רב ספרא answers that she is not forbidden. Her nearest comparison case is itself only rabbinic, and the Rabbis would not make a decree to protect a decree.
steps.simpleTranslation: רב ספרא said: She herself (the wife of the mother's brother from the father) is only forbidden by a rabbinic decree. Should we now make another decree to protect a decree?!
steps.whatsHappening: רב ספרא answers the question and says the Rabbis did not forbid this woman.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The only case she could be mixed up with is the wife of the mother's paternal half-brother. That woman is already forbidden only by the Rabbis. Forbidding the new case would mean a fence around a fence, and רב ספרא says the Rabbis do not do that.

keyTerms.meaning: She herself is only forbidden by a rabbinic decree
A decree made to protect another decree

phrases.english: Rav Safra said:
She herself is a decree,
phrases.notes: 'She' is the wife of the mother's brother from the father, the case already forbidden by the Rabbis.

phrases.english: and shall we get up and decree
a decree for a decree?!

steps.triggerLanguage: אָמַר רַב סָפְרָא: הִיא גּוּפַהּ גְּזֵירָה
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the question of step 9 by using the rule against גזירה לגזירה.
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: She is not forbidden, because forbidding her would be a גזירה לגזירה.

steps.title: רבא: the secondary relatives already work as decree upon decree
steps.stepSummary: רבא rejects רב ספרא's reasoning. The שניות themselves include decrees made because of other decrees, such as the father's mother, who is forbidden because of the mother's mother.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבא said: Are not all of these a decree for a decree? His mother is a Torah ערוה. His mother's mother is a שניה. And the Rabbis decreed on his father's mother because of his mother's mother. What is the reason? People call them all 'the grandmother's house.'
steps.whatsHappening: רבא pushes back on רב ספרא's rule and gives his first example: the grandmothers.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The mother's mother is only a rabbinic שניה, and the father's mother was forbidden to protect her. That is exactly a גזירה לגזירה. The Rabbis did it because both women go by the same family name, so people would confuse them.

keyTerms.meaning: Is that to say...? (a challenging question)
A relative forbidden by the Torah
A secondary relative forbidden by the Rabbis
'The grandmother's house,' a shared family title

phrases.english: Rava said:
Is that to say all of them are not
a decree for a decree?
His mother is a Torah-forbidden relative,
his mother's mother is a secondary relative,
and they decreed on his father's mother
because of his mother's mother.
And what is the reason?
They call them all 'the grandmother's house.'
phrases.notes: Both grandmothers go by the same name, so people would mix up which one is which.

steps.triggerLanguage: אָמַר רָבָא: אַטּוּ כּוּלְּהוּ לָאו גְּזֵירָה לִגְזֵירָה נִינְהוּ
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Rejects the rule רב ספרא relied on in step 10.
steps.dechiyaRejectionScope: רב ספרא's claim that the Rabbis never make a גזירה לגזירה among the שניות.
steps.dechiyaFlawIdentified: The father's mother is forbidden only because of the mother's mother, who is herself rabbinic. So the Rabbis do make a גזירה לגזירה when family names make confusion likely.

steps.title: Second example: the grandfathers' wives
steps.stepSummary: רבא continues with his second example. The wife of the mother's father was forbidden because of the wife of the father's father, who is herself only a שניה.
steps.simpleTranslation: His father's wife is a Torah ערוה. His father's father's wife is a שניה. And the Rabbis decreed on his mother's father's wife because of his father's father's wife. What is the reason? People call them all 'the grandfather's house.'
steps.whatsHappening: רבא gives a second case that follows the same pattern of a decree protecting a decree.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The father's father's wife is only rabbinic. Still, the mother's father's wife was forbidden to protect her, because both are called by the same family name.

keyTerms.meaning: The wife of one's mother's father
'The grandfather's house,' a shared family title

phrases.english: His father's wife is a Torah-forbidden relative,
his father's father's wife is a secondary relative,
and they decreed on his mother's father's wife
because of his father's father's wife.
And what is the reason?
They call them all 'the grandfather's house.'

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Continues רבא's proof with a second parallel case.
steps.raayaObject: That the Rabbis made a גזירה לגזירה among the שניות.
steps.raayaSupportSource: The mother's father's wife, forbidden because of the father's father's wife.

steps.title: Third example: the uncles' wives
steps.stepSummary: רבא's last example is the very family of cases in the question. The wife of the mother's paternal half-brother was itself forbidden only to protect the wife of the father's maternal half-brother, a שניה.
steps.simpleTranslation: The wife of the father's brother from the father is a Torah ערוה. The wife of the father's brother from the mother is a שניה. And the Rabbis decreed on the wife of the mother's brother from the father because of the wife of the father's brother from the mother. What is the reason? Because people call them all 'the uncle's house.'
steps.whatsHappening: רבא ends with the uncles' wives. This shows that even the case רב ספרא called 'just a decree' was itself a decree made to protect another decree.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The only Torah-level uncle's wife is the wife of the father's paternal brother. The other two were added one after the other, and the second was added because of the first. So רב ספרא's rule cannot be the reason to permit the wife of the mother's maternal half-brother.

keyTerms.meaning: The wife of the father's brother from the father (the Torah-level aunt)
'The uncle's house,' a shared family title

steps.whatToRemember: רבא shows that among the שניות the Rabbis did make decrees to protect decrees, whenever a shared family name (grandmother's house, grandfather's house, uncle's house) could cause confusion. So רב ספרא's reason for permitting the wife of the mother's maternal half-brother does not hold up.
steps.whyThisMatters: The pattern of extending a ban by a shared family name explains how the list of שניות grows beyond what the Torah forbids directly.

phrases.aramaic: אֵשֶׁת אֲחִי הָאָב מִן הָאָב — עֶרְוָה,
phrases.english: The wife of the father's brother from the father is a Torah-forbidden relative,

phrases.aramaic: אֵשֶׁת אֲחִי הָאָב מִן הָאֵם — שְׁנִיָּה,
phrases.english: the wife of the father's brother from the mother is a secondary relative,

phrases.aramaic: וְגָזְרוּ עַל אֵשֶׁת אֲחִי הָאֵם מִן הָאָב
phrases.english: and they decreed on the wife of the mother's brother from the father

phrases.aramaic: מִשּׁוּם אֵשֶׁת אֲחִי הָאָב מִן הָאֵם.
phrases.english: because of the wife of the father's brother from the mother.
And what is the reason?
Because they call them all 'the uncle's house.'

steps.triggerLanguage: אֵשֶׁת אֲחִי הָאָב מִן הָאָב — עֶרְוָה
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Finishes רבא's proof with the case closest to the question in step 9.
steps.raayaObject: That the Rabbis made a גזירה לגזירה within the very category of uncles' wives.
steps.raayaSupportSource: The wife of the mother's paternal half-brother, forbidden because of the wife of the father's maternal half-brother.

steps.title: A principle from ארץ ישראל about wives of male relatives
steps.stepSummary: With רב ספרא's answer rejected, the גמרא asks again what the law is. It brings רב יהודה בר שילא's report of a principle: for every female ערוה, the Rabbis forbade the wife of the matching male relative as a שניה.
steps.simpleTranslation: So what is the law? Come and hear: when רב יהודה בר שילא came from ארץ ישראל, he said: In the West they say, for every relative who is a Torah-forbidden relation when she is a woman, the Rabbis forbade the wife of the matching male relative, as a שניה.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא reopens the question about the wife of the mother's maternal half-brother, because רב ספרא's answer was knocked down. It brings a principle that seems to say she is forbidden.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The mother's maternal half-sister is a Torah ערוה (an aunt). The principle says that if the female relative is forbidden, the wife of the male in that same position is forbidden as a שניה. So the wife of the mother's maternal half-brother should be forbidden.

keyTerms.meaning: In the West: in ארץ ישראל
Female / male: the same family position, filled by a woman or by a man
They decreed: a rabbinic prohibition

phrases.english: What is the law? Come and hear:
phrases.notes: Since רב ספרא's answer was rejected, the question about the mother's maternal half-brother's wife is open again.

phrases.aramaic: דְּכִי אֲתָא רַב יְהוּדָה בַּר שֵׁילָא,
phrases.english: For when Rav Yehuda bar Sheila came,
he said: In the West they say:
Any relative who, as a female, is a forbidden relation,
in the male case they decreed on his wife
as a secondary relation.

steps.triggerLanguage: מַאי? תָּא שְׁמַע, דְּכִי אֲתָא רַב יְהוּדָה בַּר שֵׁילָא
steps.relationToPreviousStep: After רבא rejected רב ספרא's reasoning, the original question is open again, and a new source is brought.
steps.raayaObject: That the wife of the mother's maternal half-brother is forbidden
steps.raayaSupportSource: רב יהודה בר שילא's report of the principle taught in ארץ ישראל

steps.title: רבא shows the principle cannot be a general rule
steps.stepSummary: רבא challenges the principle by listing five cases where the female relative is a Torah ערוה, yet the wife of the matching male relative is permitted.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבא said: Is this a general rule? A man's mother-in-law is forbidden, but his father-in-law's wife is permitted. His mother-in-law's daughter is forbidden, but the wife of his mother-in-law's son is permitted. His father-in-law's daughter is forbidden, but the wife of his father-in-law's son is permitted. His stepdaughter is forbidden, but his stepson's wife is permitted. His stepdaughter's daughter is forbidden, but the wife of his stepson's son is permitted.
steps.whatsHappening: רבא attacks the principle by showing many cases that break it. All of them are relatives through marriage.
steps.deeperAnalysis: In each pair, the woman is a Torah ערוה, but the wife of the man in the matching position is allowed. So the principle cannot be a rule that covers everything. This puts the proof from step 14 in doubt.

keyTerms.meaning: A general rule
His mother-in-law / his father-in-law
His stepdaughter / his stepson: his wife's children from another man
Permitted

steps.confusionAlert: Do not mix up the pairs. The first woman in each pair is forbidden by the Torah. The second woman, the wife of the matching male relative, is completely permitted.

phrases.english: And Rava said: Is this a general rule?
His mother-in-law is a forbidden relation, yet his father-in-law's wife is permitted.
phrases.notes: This is the father-in-law's other wife, not one's own mother-in-law.

phrases.english: His mother-in-law's daughter is a forbidden relation,
yet the wife of his mother-in-law's son is permitted.
His father-in-law's daughter is a forbidden relation,
yet the wife of his father-in-law's son is permitted.
His stepdaughter is a forbidden relation, yet his stepson's wife is permitted.
His stepdaughter's daughter is a forbidden relation,
yet the wife of his stepson's son is permitted!

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Challenges the principle brought in step 14 as a general rule.
steps.kashyaTarget: רב יהודה בר שילא's principle that every female ערוה makes the matching male relative's wife a שניה
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: Five in-law cases have a female ערוה while the matching male relative's wife is permitted, so the principle cannot be universal.

steps.title: The principle exists to include our case
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא answers that the principle is not a general rule. It was said to include one specific case: the wife of the mother's maternal half-brother.
steps.simpleTranslation: Then what does רב יהודה בר שילא's statement come to include? Doesn't it come to include the wife of the mother's maternal half-brother? Since every female relative who is a forbidden relation makes the matching male relative's wife forbidden as a שניה.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא keeps the principle alive by limiting it. It must have been said to teach about our exact case.
steps.deeperAnalysis: רבא proved the principle is not true everywhere. So the statement must have a specific purpose, and that purpose is the case in question. The mother's maternal half-sister is a Torah ערוה, so the wife of her brother is a שניה. This answers the question from step 9: she is forbidden.

keyTerms.meaning: To include: to teach a case that would otherwise be left out
The wife of one's mother's brother who shares only a mother with her

steps.whatToRemember: The wife of the mother's maternal half-brother is a rabbinic שניה. רב יהודה בר שילא's principle was said for her.

phrases.english: And that statement of Rav Yehuda bar Sheila,
what does it come to include?

phrases.aramaic: לָאו לְאֵיתוֹיֵי אֵשֶׁת אֲחִי הָאֵם מִן הָאֵם,
phrases.english: Is it not to include the wife of the mother's maternal half-brother,
since for any relative who, as a female, is a forbidden relation,
in the male case they decreed on his wife as a secondary relation?

steps.triggerLanguage: וְהָא דְּרַב יְהוּדָה בַּר שֵׁילָא לְאֵיתוֹיֵי מַאי?
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers רבא's challenge by limiting the principle to one specific case, which settles the question from step 9.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Limiting the scope of a statement to a specific case
steps.terutzHavaAmina: The principle seemed to be a general rule, and רבא disproved it.
steps.terutzMaskana: The principle was said to include the wife of the mother's maternal half-brother, so she is a שניה.

steps.title: Why is our case different from the in-law cases?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא asks what makes the in-law cases permitted and the wife of the mother's maternal half-brother forbidden.
steps.simpleTranslation: What is different about these cases, and what is different about this case?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא asks for the reason behind the difference. Its answer comes in the next step.
steps.deeperAnalysis: If the principle works for the mother's half-brother's wife, why does it not work for the father-in-law's wife and the other cases רבא listed? Without a reason, the distinction looks random.

keyTerms.meaning: What is different: a request for the reason two cases are treated differently

phrases.aramaic: מַאי שְׁנָא הָנֵי, וּמַאי שְׁנָא הָא?
phrases.english: What is different about these, and what is different about this?
phrases.notes: "These" are רבא's in-law cases; "this" is the wife of the mother's maternal half-brother.

steps.triggerLanguage: מַאי שְׁנָא הָנֵי, וּמַאי שְׁנָא הָא?
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Questions the distinction made in step 16 between our case and רבא's cases.
steps.kashyaTarget: The distinction between the in-law cases and the mother's maternal half-brother's wife
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: Both look like the same pattern of a female ערוה next to the matching male relative's wife, so treating them differently needs a reason.

steps.title: One marriage versus two marriages
steps.stepSummary: The wife of the mother's half-brother is connected to the man through one marriage. The in-law cases are connected only through two marriages, so the Rabbis did not decree on them.
steps.simpleTranslation: This one is brought close through one marriage. These others are not brought close unless there are two marriages.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers the question by counting how many marriages link the man to the woman.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The man's uncle is a blood relative, so the uncle's wife is linked to him through one marriage, the uncle's. For the father-in-law's wife you need two marriages: the man's marriage to his own wife, and the father-in-law's marriage. A link that far away was not close enough for the Rabbis to forbid.

keyTerms.meaning: One act of betrothal: one marriage creates the link
Two acts of betrothal: two marriages are needed to create the link
Brings close: makes her a relative

steps.whatToRemember: The Rabbis made a שניה only where one marriage connects the woman to a blood relative. Where two marriages are needed, she stays permitted.
steps.whyThisMatters: This gives a clear test for which wives of relatives the Rabbis forbade, and it explains all of רבא's counterexamples.

phrases.english: This one is brought close through a single betrothal,
phrases.notes: The uncle is a blood relative, so only his own marriage links his wife to the nephew.

phrases.english: these, until there are two betrothals,
are not brought close.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the question of step 17 by explaining the difference.
steps.terutzHavaAmina: All relatives' wives seem to follow the same pattern, so the in-law cases and our case look alike.
steps.terutzMaskana: A link through one marriage makes a שניה. A link through two marriages does not.

steps.title: רב משרשיא asks about the generation above
steps.stepSummary: רב משרשיא asks רב פפי whether the wife of the father's father's brother and the father's father's sister are forbidden as שניות.
steps.simpleTranslation: רב משרשיא from תוסניא sent a question to רב פפי: Teach us, our master. What is the law about the wife of the father's father's brother and the sister of the father's father? One generation below, these relatives are a Torah ערוה, so maybe the Rabbis also decreed on the generation above. Or maybe, once the generations are separate, they did not decree.
steps.whatsHappening: A new question opens. רב משרשיא asks whether two relatives one generation higher than a Torah ערוה are forbidden by the Rabbis.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The father's sister and the wife of the father's brother are a Torah ערוה. The question is whether the Rabbis went up one more generation and forbade the grandfather's sister and the wife of the grandfather's brother. One side says the closeness to a Torah ערוה is enough for a גזירה. The other side says the extra generation creates a break.

keyTerms.meaning: Let our master teach us. A polite way of opening a question to a teacher.
Since below it is a forbidden relation. Here it means one generation lower.
Above, meaning one generation higher.
The generations have separated, so the link is broken.

phrases.english: Rav Mesharshiya from Tusneya sent a message
to Rav Pappi:
Let our master teach us:
the wife of the father's father's brother,
and the sister of the father's father, what is the law?
Since below it is a forbidden relation,
phrases.notes: 'Below' means one generation down: the father's sister and the father's brother's wife are forbidden by the Torah (ויקרא 18:12, 18:14).

phrases.english: did they also decree on it above?
Or perhaps
the generations have separated.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: After the explanation of why the Rabbis decreed on the wife of the mother's maternal half-brother, a new question asks how far upward the שניות go.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: Are the wife of the father's father's brother and the father's father's sister forbidden as שניות?

steps.title: Proof from the list that leaves them out
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא tries to prove these women are permitted, because the ברייתא listing the שניות does not include them.
steps.simpleTranslation: Come and hear: the ברייתא asks, 'What are the שניות?' and it does not count these two women among them.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא tries to answer the question from a ברייתא it quoted earlier. That ברייתא lists the שניות and does not mention these two women.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The proof argues from silence. If the list of שניות were complete, leaving these women out would mean they are permitted.

keyTerms.meaning: Secondary forbidden relatives, forbidden by the Rabbis.
He counts or lists.

phrases.english: Come and hear:
"What are the secondary relations?"
and it does not count them among them!

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Tries to answer רב משרשיא's question.
steps.raayaObject: That the wife of the father's father's brother and the father's father's sister are permitted.
steps.raayaSupportSource: The ברייתא 'מה הן שניות', which does not list them.

steps.title: The list was not complete
steps.stepSummary: The proof is rejected: the תנא taught some cases and left others out.
steps.simpleTranslation: The תנא taught some cases and left some out.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא pushes back on the proof. A list that leaves something out does not prove that the missing case is permitted.
steps.deeperAnalysis: An argument from silence only works if the list is complete. If the תנא left cases out, these two women could simply be among the missing ones.

keyTerms.meaning: He taught and left out. The list is not complete.

phrases.english: He taught and left some out.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Rejects the proof brought in step 20.
steps.dechiyaRejectionScope: The proof from the ברייתא's silence.
steps.dechiyaFlawIdentified: It assumes the list is complete, but the תנא may have left cases out.

steps.title: What else did he leave out?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא challenges the claim: if the תנא left something out, what else did he leave out besides this?
steps.simpleTranslation: What else did he leave out, that we should say he left this out too?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא challenges the rejection. Before saying the תנא skipped these cases, it wants to see another case he skipped.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The גמרא works with an assumption that a תנא does not leave out just one case. To claim he skipped these women, you must show that he also skipped other cases.

keyTerms.meaning: What else did he leave out, that he also left this out?

steps.confusionAlert: This line does not deny that the list is incomplete. It only asks for another missing case to back up the claim.

phrases.english: What else did he leave out, that he left this out?

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Challenges the תנא ושייר answer of step 21.
steps.kashyaTarget: The claim that the ברייתא left these two cases out.
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: Claiming that something was left out needs another clear example of something left out.

steps.title: He left out the list of רבי חייא's school
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא answers that the תנא left out the whole list of שניות taught by רבי חייא's school.
steps.simpleTranslation: He left out the שניות of רבי חייא's school.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers the challenge. It names other cases the תנא left out: the list of שניות taught by רבי חייא's school.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Since a whole group of שניות is clearly missing from the ברייתא, the list is clearly not complete. So the silence about these two women proves nothing, and the attempted proof fails. The next step brings אמימר's ruling on the question.

keyTerms.meaning: Of the school (study house) of רבי חייא.

phrases.english: He left out the secondary relations of the school of Rabbi Chiya.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the challenge of step 22.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Identifies another omission to show the list is incomplete.
steps.terutzHavaAmina: The ברייתא's list seemed complete, so these women would be permitted.
steps.terutzMaskana: The ברייתא left out רבי חייא's list too, so it cannot decide the question.

steps.title: אמימר permits these two relatives
steps.stepSummary: אמימר rules that the wife of the father's father's brother and the father's father's sister are permitted.
steps.simpleTranslation: אמימר permitted the wife of one's father's father's brother and the sister of one's father's father.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא brings a ruling on the open question. אמימר permitted both women.
steps.deeperAnalysis: אמימר takes the side that the extra generation breaks the link, so the Rabbis did not decree here. This sets up the challenge that comes next.

keyTerms.meaning: Permitted. He declared them fit to marry.
His father's father, his grandfather.

phrases.english: Ameimar permitted
the wife of his father's father's brother
and his father's father's sister.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Gives a ruling on the question that the proof failed to settle.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: The wife of the father's father's brother and the father's father's sister are permitted.

steps.title: רב הלל's count of sixteen
steps.stepSummary: רב הלל challenges אמימר: מר בריה דרבנא's list has sixteen forbidden שניות, and the count seems to include these two women.
steps.simpleTranslation: רב הלל said to רב אשי: I myself saw the list of שניות of מר בריה דרבנא, and sixteen were written there as forbidden. Isn't this the eight of the ברייתא, plus the six of רבי חייא's school, plus these two? That makes sixteen.
steps.whatsHappening: רב הלל challenges אמימר's ruling with a written list he saw. He adds up the numbers to show that these two women were counted as forbidden.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Eight from the ברייתא plus six from רבי חייא's school makes fourteen. Two more are needed to reach sixteen, and these two women fit exactly. If so, they are forbidden, against אמימר. The next step pushes back on this count.

keyTerms.meaning: I myself saw it.
Sixteen.
Is it not? Introduces a suggested reading.
A teaching of the תנאים. Here it means the ברייתא.

phrases.aramaic: אָמַר לֵיהּ רַב הִלֵּל לְרַב אָשֵׁי:
phrases.english: Rav Hillel said to Rav Ashi:
I myself saw
the secondary relations of Mar son of Rabbana,
and sixteen were written as forbidden.
Is it not:
eight of the baraita,
and six of the school of Rabbi Chiya,
and these two
phrases.notes: These are the two women אמימר permitted.

phrases.english: that makes sixteen.

steps.triggerLanguage: לְדִידִי חַזְיָא לִי שְׁנִיּוֹת מָר בְּרֵיהּ דְּרַבְנָא
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Challenges אמימר's ruling in step 24.
steps.kashyaTarget: אמימר's ruling that the two women are permitted.
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: 8 + 6 = 14. The two extra cases needed to reach 16 seem to be exactly these two women, so they were written as forbidden.

steps.title: Your way of counting would give seventeen, not sixteen
steps.stepSummary: Using רב הלל's own logic, the count of forbidden שניות would come to seventeen, because the wife of the mother's maternal brother was also ruled forbidden.
steps.simpleTranslation: And by your reasoning, there would be seventeen, because there is also the wife of the mother's maternal brother, whom we already ruled is forbidden!
steps.whatsHappening: The reply defends אמימר by turning רב הלל's argument back on him. If the list of sixteen had to include every forbidden שנייה, the number would not add up.
steps.deeperAnalysis: רב הלל said the sixteen must include אמימר's two women. But earlier the גמרא ruled that the wife of the mother's maternal brother is also forbidden, and she would push the total to seventeen. So the number sixteen cannot prove what רב הלל wants. מר בריה דרבנא's list was not meant to count every possible case.

keyTerms.meaning: And according to your reasoning: an argument that uses the other side's own logic against him
Seventeen
The wife of the mother's brother who shares only their mother
We resolved (a question that had been left open)
As forbidden

steps.confusionAlert: This line does not say she is permitted. It agrees she is forbidden. The point is only that she is missing from the count, so the number sixteen is not a complete list.

phrases.english: And according to your reasoning: there would be seventeen,
since there is also
the wife of the mother's maternal brother,
whom we resolved to be forbidden!

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Counters רב הלל's challenge (step 25) by turning his counting logic against him.
steps.kashyaTarget: רב הלל's claim that the number sixteen proves that אמימר's two women are forbidden.
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: If the count included every forbidden case, the wife of the mother's maternal brother, already ruled forbidden, would make it seventeen. So the count cannot be a complete list.

steps.title: Opening the answer: this is not a difficulty
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא begins to answer on behalf of רב הלל, declaring that the seventeen problem is not a real difficulty.
steps.simpleTranslation: This is not difficult.
steps.whatsHappening: This is a setup line. The גמרא announces that the seventeen problem can be answered, and the explanation continues on the next amud.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The reply has not given its reason yet. It only signals that רב הלל's count of sixteen can still work. The continuation on the next amud explains why the wife of the mother's maternal brother does not break the count.

keyTerms.meaning: This is not difficult: the opening words of an answer

phrases.english: This is not difficult,

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Begins answering the seventeen problem raised in step 26, defending רב הלל's count.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Opening of a defense; the actual reason follows in the next line.
steps.terutzHavaAmina: It seemed that the extra forbidden case makes seventeen, so the count of sixteen could not include אמימר's two women.
steps.terutzMaskana: The count of sixteen can still be defended. The explanation follows.
